title: Economic Promotion Agencies Merge to Support Companies' Growth
what_it_is: Economic Promotion Agencies Merge to Support Companies' Growth

sections.label: SPRING and IE merger
sections.summary: The merger of SPRING and IE forms Enterprise Singapore, aiming to better meet companies' needs by combining both agencies' resources.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Last week, I announced the merger of SPRING and IE to form a new Government agency, Enterprise Singapore, which aims to better meet the needs of companies in this dynamic economic environment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Industry) (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We will be able to do more for and with our enterprises by leveraging the combined resources and levers of both SPRING and IE Singapore.

sections.label: Companies assisted by agencies
sections.summary: SPRING assisted about 22,000 companies a year and IE Singapore about 34,000, prompting a question on the merged entity's focus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SPRING assisted about 22,000 companies a year and IE Singapore about 34,000 a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These are very impressive numbers and credit to the two organisations for helping out the SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask the Minister: following the merger of the two agencies, whether the focus will continue to be to grow the number of companies assisted, or that the merged entity will dedicate more resources and support to high-growth enterprises which are scaling up or internationalising and will tend to create more jobs, better jobs.

sections.label: Smooth transition priority
sections.summary: The highest priority is a smooth transition, with the objective being to strengthen support for enterprises across their evolution stages.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On the first, I want to emphasise, first and foremost, the highest priority in this process is to ensure a smooth transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I note that there may be some concerns about this.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But in fact, the objective of the exercise is to strengthen the way we are able to work with enterprises and to afford them a greater continuum of support across different stages of their evolution.

sections.label: Mission and CEO choice
sections.summary: The mission is to create globally competitive Singapore enterprises with deep capabilities, guiding the choice of the CEO-designate.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, this is where the focus is on getting the mission and leadership right in the first instance because, if we cannot get that clear, then it will be much harder to follow through.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I have already stated what the mission is, and to restate it, it is really to create globally competitive Singapore enterprises which have deep capabilities, and that applies to the whole range of enterprises from startups to scale-ups and large local enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This will guide the ethos and culture in their work and the programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: This is why we have been very deliberate in the choice of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO)-designate who is the current Second Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Trade and Industry but he has also got extensive experience through SPRING Singapore where he was CEO previously and also JTC, and he was CEO there as well.
